parts.text:
Mitya appears to have something on his mind...

#### Talk to Mitya

**Paimon:** Mitya, why are you standing here spacing out all by yourself?

**Mitya:** Paimon, Traveler, there's something I'd like to ask for your thoughts on.

**Mitya:** Here's what happened...

**Mitya:** Before leaving Snezhnograd, I told Mr. Valeriy that I'd be staying near Novokitezhgrad for a while. As you know, some of his work is connected to mine.

**Mitya:** When we met that day, I noticed a bottle of wine sitting on his desk. It looked strangely familiar, so I couldn't help taking a closer look.

**Mitya:** It was a gift from one of his colleagues. Apparently, it had been open for quite some time, but there was still plenty left. He said the flavor felt somewhat... unusual to him, so he simply left it there.

**Paimon:** Hmm... Are you trying to say Valeriy was acting a bit strange, or something?

**Mitya:** No, I mean it just occurred to me why the bottle looked familiar.

**Mitya:** That bottle of Snowy Nocturne on his desk is one of this winery's best-sellers. If I actually drank alcohol, I probably would have noticed much sooner.

**Paimon:** Ah, but you're not the type to check this stuff out, so...

**Mitya:** Exactly. But once I did, I started smelling a rat.

**Mitya:** Due to an ingredient shortage, this winery has been unable to produce it for at least half a year.

**Mitya:** I just asked Mr. Urkin, and even their final shipment was quite limited in scale. So, wine like this should have disappeared from the market long ago...

**Mitya:** But Valeriy's colleague bought it only recently. Isn't that a bit odd?

**Mitya:** So when he said the taste was unusual... perhaps he wasn't talking about the flavor alone. Perhaps there was something wrong with the wine.

**Paimon:** You mean... they bought some sorta counterfeit?

**Mitya:** Yes. It was just a wild guess at first, but Mr. Urkin confirmed my suspicions, saying that there are indeed counterfeits of unknown origin circulating on the market.

**Mitya:** He once mentioned that the winery's income had dropped sharply in recent years. Looking back, I think he might not have known how to bring up the matter of counterfeit goods.

- **Traveler:** Then we should look into this.

**Mitya:** You actually think so? Nice. I was just considering how I might get you on our side.

**Mitya:** No time to lose. I've already contacted Valeriy and asked him to come find us here with that bottle of wine.

**Mitya:** Let's walk to the station and wait for him.

#### Meet with Valeriy

Before long, Valeriy arrives with the minecart, bringing that bottle of wine as a sample...

Mitya also shares all the relevant information from earlier...

**Valeriy:** This is quite the unexpected development.

**Valeriy:** From our perspective, Snowy Nocturne was never discontinued.

**Mitya:** That seems about right. Can't expect consumers to keep constant track of a product's production status.

**Valeriy:** True. But this also proves two other things — that our counterfeiters have a very wide distribution network, and that this illegal business has persisted for quite some time.

**Paimon:** Looks like things are more serious than we thought.

**Valeriy:** Agreed.

**Valeriy:** Mr. Urkin should have an authentic sample with him. We should compare them.

**Mitya:** He should be in at this hour. Let's go find him.

#### Ask Urkin for information

**Mitya:** Mr. Urkin.

**Valeriy:** Mr. Urkin? Excuse me. We have something we'd like to ask you about.

**Urkin:** Ah! My goodness, I'm so sorry... Sir, I meant no offense. I just didn't expect an officer to drop by so suddenly...

**Mitya:** Haha, relax. This is Valeriy, an upright and responsible man, and a friend of mine.

**Mitya:** We discovered that bottles of Snowy Nocturne, which should've been discontinued, have been appearing on the market. This bottle in Valeriy's possession was purchased recently, and we'd like to compare it with the original.

**Mitya:** You should still have a sample of the authentic version here, correct? Would it be possible to take a look?

**Valeriy:** We say "take a look," but in truth, it'll mean opening a bottle. I apologize for making such a sudden request.

**Urkin:** Oh, no, no, Sir, please don't say that. Honestly, I... I never expected anyone to pay attention to this matter.

**Urkin:** We kept a few sample bottles from the previous batches. I believe they should be stored over there... Ah, here they are.

**Urkin:** It's nothing fancy, but please, give it a taste. This is what the original was supposed to be.

**Valeriy:** ...As expected, it tastes completely different from the counterfeit.

**Valeriy:** From how you speak of this... did you already know about the illegal goods entering the market?

**Urkin:** Uh... about that...

**Mitya:** Mr. Urkin, if you've ever experienced any difficulties because of this, I assure you — Valeriy is nothing like those officials you may have dealt with before.

**Urkin:** Ahaha... is it really that obvious?

**Mitya:** Pardon my frankness, but you've never been good at lying. And in my opinion, that's actually a good thing.

**Urkin:** That's true, that's true... *sigh* We've known about the bootleg liquor for a long time, and even reported it to the relevant authorities, but we never received any meaningful response.

**Urkin:** Everyone knows what Snezhnaya has been like these past few years. Every department is under pressure, and there simply weren't enough people to deal with what seemed like a minor issue...

**Mitya:** Ah... I don't think anyone could call this a minor issue at this point.

**Valeriy:** I believe this matter requires a proper investigation.

**Urkin:** Truly? You... you're willing to spend your time on something involving such a small winery?

**Valeriy:** Yes.

**Valeriy:** I once thought I wasn't the sort of person to enjoy Snowy Nocturne. But after trying the original today, I realize that was a misapprehension.

**Valeriy:** Just consider it a small favor for this bottle of wine, sir.

**Paimon:** Yeah, we're just helping make sure everyone gets a fair shot, right?

**Urkin:** Thank you, truly. Thank you all.

**Mitya:** That said, we have very few clues right now, so we'll need to ask around some more. Mr. Urkin, is there any other related matter you can think of?

**Urkin:** Please, give me a moment... Let me think...

**Kolov:** Mr. Urkin, sir! Did you see? That person came again... Ah!

**Kolov:** I'm so sorry. I—I didn't realize you had guests.

**Urkin:** Kolov, are you saying that person came again? Goodness, what on earth is he after?

**Mitya:** "Again?"

**Kolov:** Mr. Mitya, you probably don't know this, but there's been a stranger wandering about near our winery lately, always watching and keeping an eye on things...

**Valeriy:** Where is he now?

**Kolov:** Right on the other side of the fence.

**Mitya:** This person might be connected to the case. We should bring him in!

#### Look for the suspicious person

**Mitya:** Hey! Hey, you over there!

**???:** Whoa! What... why are you all rushing over here!

**Valeriy:** Excuse me. Do you mind if we ask you a few questions?

**???:** A military officer? You... ahem. Fine, ask your questions.

**Valeriy:** May I ask your name?

**Staranov:** You can call me Staranov.

**Valeriy:** (Staranov... Sounds familiar.)

**Valeriy:** What are you doing here?

**Staranov:** Sir, what am I to say? I'm a Snezhnayan standing on Snezhnayan land that isn't closed off to the public. I don't need a special reason to be here.

**Valeriy:** But sometimes, people who linger in the same place for a long time usually have reasons they don't wish others to know about.

**Staranov:** What? No! I don't have any hidden intentions. I'm just... looking for someone.

**Mitya:** If you don't have anyone to introduce you, I can help arrange a meeting with the owner here. Seeing as you've been here this long, I'm sure you already know his name.

**Staranov:** ...

**Staranov:** I... I'm sorry, I can't go to him directly.

**Staranov:** This is a family matter... I'm looking for my daughter. I heard someone saw her around here, so I came to check.

**Valeriy:** And that's why you're surveilling this winery?

**Staranov:** Surveilling? Oh, no, no, I'm just... investigating! Yes, investigating.

**Staranov:** My daughter has always been a little mischievous. Realistically, she wouldn't stay somewhere like this for long. And sure enough, she isn't here. But... *sigh* I just can't find her.

**Staranov:** I can't find her, do you understand? Maybe I'm just standing here pretending she's still nearby. Maybe I'm missing her, alright? Either way, I'm really sorry.

**Staranov:** The winery staff must have sent you. Well, honestly... they're good people. They've never bothered me or made things difficult.

**Staranov:** ...I'm sorry. I never meant to disturb any of you. I'll leave now.

As Staranov says this, a hint of sadness crossing his face. Perhaps he is thinking of his daughter. Not long after, he quietly takes his leave.

**Mitya:** What do you guys think?

**Paimon:** He says he's looking for his daughter, but something feels off... Then again, he doesn't look like he's completely lying.

- **Traveler:** We can't ascertain this person's intentions yet.

**Valeriy:** He's definitely hiding something. But not everything he said was a lie... One thing is certain: he's been investigating something.

**Mitya:** I was thinking the same thing. It's not so much that he's suspicious... It feels more like he's suspicious of someone else.

**Mitya:** And from the looks of him, he really doesn't seem to know Mr. Urkin... Hmm. None of this counts as a solid lead yet.

**Valeriy:** So what's our next move?

**Mitya:** Looking at the crops and the brewing conditions, the counterfeit wine was probably produced somewhere near Novokitezhgrad as well. And if they want to sell it...

**Mitya:** They'll have to use the local distribution channels. There may be clues in the city.

**Valeriy:** We don't have many people to spare. With our current numbers, it would be better to be discreet.

**Valeriy:** Places like taverns probably have informants from bootlegging gangs. Just to be safe, let's head to the market street and ask around first.

#### Go to Novokitezhgrad

**Mitya:** We've arrived at the market street. Mr. Officer, if anyone needs to keep a low profile right now, it's you.

**Valeriy:** A soldier sneaking around would probably look even more out of place. Just think of it as me escorting you. Nothing unusual about that.

**Mitya:** Oh, fine. Having you as an escort despite clearly being on vacation... Feels like I'm back on duty again... *sigh*

**Valeriy:** Consider it an unexpected challenge, Mr. Mitya. Besides, you can't deny that having me here makes things safer.

**Mitya:** Of course... Hmm?

**Paimon:** Hey, isn't that guy over there the one from just now... Uh, what was his name again, Sta... Staranov?

**Valeriy:** It seems he is having some trouble.

**Staranov:** Why won't you let me in? This isn't even private property!

**Vicious Police Officer:** It's closed off. I'll say it again — it's closed! Do you understand?

**Greasy Police Officer:** In special situations, the Transport Bureau has the authority to block off certain roads to keep citizens away, especially suspicious individuals. Isn't that right, Staranov?

**Staranov:** ...You!

**Valeriy:** Did I hear mention of "special circumstances" a moment ago? May I ask what happened here?

**Greasy Police Officer:** What? Who're you... Huh?

**Vicious Police Officer:** Someone from the military...

**Valeriy:** I am Major Valeriy, Leader of the Special Assignments Battalion, Armory Palace Royal Grenadier Guards, First Regiment. Do you require assistance here?

**Vicious Police Officer:** Major!? Ah... um, no, no, no, it's nothing like that, Sir. All just a misunderstanding.

**Valeriy:** But I believe I just heard you say this area had been sealed off.

**Vicious Police Officer:** A complete misunderstanding, Sir. There... There's just some shops back here, and we're... doing a routine inspection.

**Greasy Police Officer:** That's right, a routine inspection!

**Valeriy:** So, if I understand correctly... there's nothing unusual happening here, and ordinary citizens are free to pass through this area. Is that right?

**Greasy Police Officer:** Yes, yes. Exactly.

**Vicious Police Officer:** The inspection's done. We'll be taking our leave.

**Paimon:** Those two were totally just picking on that old man, weren't they?

**Mitya:** Yeah, I wonder what kind of history they have... Hmm? Wait, where did that old gentleman go?

**Valeriy:** Must've slipped away while we were distracted.

**Valeriy:** ...Staranov... I'm sure I've heard that name somewhere. Or maybe even seen him before.

- **Traveler:** Someone you're familiar with?

**Valeriy:** Yes. And it doesn't bring up any unpleasant memories, either. That's why I decided to help him just now.

**Mitya:** And he didn't even say thank you! Next time I run into him, I'm definitely asking what that was all about.

**Valeriy:** Someone of his age, with connections to the Transport Bureau... Could he be...

**???:** Huh. What a surprise, meeting you in Novokitezhgrad. All at once, and together, no less.

**Paimon:** Huh?

**Mitya:** Vodyanitsa? Odette?

**Odette:** Hello there.

- **Traveler:** Good afternoon. How have you been?

**Vodyanitsa:** How have we been, you say? Odette, how do you think we've been doing?

**Odette:** Should our situations be lumped together like that?

**Vodyanitsa:** The two of us were invited to Novokitezhgrad in our capacity as onstage partners. So, no matter how you look at it, we're a package deal.

**Mitya:** Is some sort of performance being staged here?

**Vodyanitsa:** No, no, just a charity gala tonight. We don't even have to perform. The gentleman hosting it isn't the type to force anyone to do things they'd prefer not to.

**Odette:** Seems like you weren't invited here by Mr. Denngiyev. He's the local wealthy merchant she just spoke of.

**Mitya:** Well, given my position and Valeriy's rank, such events are definitely out of our league. The only ones present who might've been are probably...

**Paimon:** Why are you looking at us? This is the first we're hearing of this!

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** My generosity...

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Wouldn't quite qualify me for an invitation...

##### Shared continuation

**Odette:** I wouldn't say that. People at charity galas aren't always invited for their altruism.

**Vodyanitsa:** Oh, come on. Is that your way of secretly talking yourself up while looking modest? If you ask me, the Novokitezhgrad bigwigs just didn't expect you to show up.

**Vodyanitsa:** If they'd known, you'd have received an invitation before you could say "opera." A win-win deal for all, you understand.

**Vodyanitsa:** For all of you to show up together at once... Has something happened here? A case worth looking into, maybe?

**Mitya:** Ah, clever as always. Nothing gets past you. Then why don't you take another guess? Where do you think we're headed to next?

**Odette:** To ask us for a favor, I bet.

**Mitya:** Oh, it'll be well worth your time, dear ladies. I'd be happy to treat you to a lovely meal. All I ask is that you two honor me with your company.

You tell Odette and Vodyanitsa everything about your ongoing investigation into the illegal wine trade...

**Odette:** They'd never serve drinks of that quality at a charity gala like this. But the attendees... All names worth remembering. It might be worth a shot.

**Vodyanitsa:** Those of us who received invitations are allowed to bring attendants or companions. If you're willing, you can accompany us.

**Vodyanitsa:** Considering your fame and reputation, I doubt anyone no will question it.

**Valeriy:** An excellent idea, Miss.

**Mitya:** What do you guys think?

- **Traveler:** Sounds reasonable to me.

**Paimon:** Paimon's cool with it! We can head out right now if you want!

**Odette:** That's our plan, then.

#### Wait for the banquet to begin

**Cerny:** Hehe, time to get to work again.

#### Enter the banquet

**Vodyanitsa:** It's almost time, everyone. Let's head in.

Following Vodyanitsa and Odette's lead, your party successfully enter the charity gala held tonight in Novokitezhgrad.

**Paimon:** Wow, there's so many people here... And look at all this food! Hehe.

- **Traveler:** You can have a little, but don't forget why we're here, alright?

**Paimon:** Aw, don't you worry!

**Mitya:** Let's split up and ask around. And we'll meet up at the banquet hall entrance later. Sound good?

**Paimon:** You got it!

**Valeriy:** Works for me.

**Mitya:** I just checked. There are some military personnel here. They're all yours, Mr. Valeriy. Try to learn as much from them as you can.

**Valeriy:** Sure.

**Mitya:** I see a few merchants over there. Familiar faces. They've probably supplied the Armory Palace and the Commission before. I'll handle chatting them up.

**Mitya:** Traveler, Paimon, you're both old hands at gathering intel, so I'll let you do your thing.

**Mitya:** Events like this tend to attract government officials and influential figures as well. With your current status, not to mention how you've caught Her Majesty's eye, I'd say...

- **Traveler:** We'll handle that.

**Mitya:** Couldn't hope for more. Looks like our little team really does cover every angle!

**Valeriy:** Miss Vodyanitsa and Miss Odette have their own social obligations to attend to. We shouldn't trouble them.

**Valeriy:** Everyone, let's begin. We'll regroup in an hour.

#### Talk to the guests at the banquet and gather clues

- **Traveler:** (Come to think of it, this might be my first time attending an event like this... Quite a few people are stealing glances at me, but no one's come over to start a conversation.)

- **Traveler:** (Merchants, politicians, officials... Adept conversationalists, one and all. By contrast, Paimon and I stick out like sore thumbs.)

**???:** I was told that some interesting news awaited me here. I didn't think it would be you, dear guest.

**Paimon:** The Rooster? Huh. Paimon didn't hear that a Harbinger was invited to this party!

**The Rooster:** It appears your impression of me begins with my role as Harbinger, rather than as mayor. In truth, I'm only here to discuss a few administrative matters.

**The Rooster:** Mining collaborations and public affairs management... Such topics never go out of fashion at gatherings like this. Dull, perhaps, but necessary. Much like myself.

**The Rooster:** I presume you arrived with the two ladies from the Korolevskiy Theater.

**Paimon:** Good guess! Nothing gets past you, huh?

**The Rooster:** The social circles of younger people at such gatherings are always somewhat more free-form. And if those connections should last... Well, I stand to benefit from that, too.

**The Rooster:** Sometimes, stable relationships mean stable alliances. Older people tend to abandon such ties when they no longer need them... only to seek them out again when they age further still.

- **Traveler:** Do you mean to say that older Snezhnayan groups are less reliable than the younger generation?

**The Rooster:** Allow me to answer politely: Yes, and even one as old as I must confront such issues.

**The Rooster:** Should you ever run into trouble, don't hesitate to come to me. I could make assuaging your anxieties my business.

**Paimon:** Really? You may be joking, Mr. Mayor, but we're gonna take you at your word, y'know!

**The Rooster:** Oh, believe me, I'd much rather you do invest such trust in me.

- **Traveler:** (Speaking of which... Mr. Urkin mentioned that the issues he reported were never properly addressed. It seems this might be the perfect chance to bring that up.)

- **Traveler:** In that case... We and Mitya, a researcher from the Energy Commission, encountered a certain situation. Allow me to explain, Sir...

You briefly explain the trouble the winery has been facing due to the spread of bootleg wine...

**The Rooster:** Now, this may not seem like much in the face of our present circumstances. But it is most regrettable nonetheless.

- **Traveler:** I concur. Still... why did this matter never make it any further up the chain?

**The Rooster:** Goodness, such a serious question for this casual banquet. Still, I see that this matter stands in the way of your journey, and there is no chance you shall simply let it go.

**The Rooster:** Your friend, Major Valeriy, would likely give you a very straightforward answer to this question. I, too, understand what you mean to say.

**The Rooster:** The departments responsible should be ashamed of how this was handled. I'll have someone look into it. You have my word.

**Paimon:** Great! Guess Mr. Urkin and Mrs. Sezhna can finally relax a little!

- **Traveler:** This is unexpected... Thank you so much, Mr. Rooster.

**The Rooster:** Think nothing of it. Your gratitude, however lightly given, is already the best gift you might have given this banquet, and me.

**The Rooster:** Ah. It seems I am being called away. Enjoy your evening, dear guests. Please excuse me.

#### Talk to the guests at the banquet and gather clues

**Military Officer:** Major Valeriy! I didn't expect to see you here.

**Valeriy:** Good evening, Sir.

**Military Officer:** You came on Mr. Denngiyev's invitation, I take it?

**Valeriy:** Yes. I am responsible for ensuring the safety of Miss Vodyanitsa, Miss Odette, and Mr. Mitya tonight.

**Military Officer:** I see. Makes sense that they'd call upon someone like you.

**Valeriy:** You flatter me, Sir.

**Valeriy:** By the way, on my way here, I ran into some Transport Bureau officers. And regarding that...

#### Talk to the guests at the banquet and gather clues

**Denngiyev:** Ah, you must be the brilliant researcher from the Energy Commission that Miss Vodyanitsa and Miss Odette mentioned! A promising young talent indeed, I see!

**Mitya:** Had you mentioned the Commission, I wouldn't have believed you were talking about me. I wasn't expecting personal mention.

**Mitya:** Allow me to properly introduce myself — Mitya, Energy Commission researcher. It's a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Denngiyev.

**Denngiyev:** Hahahaha! Your presence is a surprise, yes, but a most pleasant one! Come, come, choose any drink you like. Let's have a proper chat.

**Mitya:** Oh, of course. I've also been looking forward to meeting you ever since these two fine ladies mentioned you.

**Mitya:** I'm actually quite curious about Novokitezhgrad, and I've thrown together a few questions I'd like to consult you on.

**Vodyanitsa:** Want some more? If you ask me, you're already in great shape. A little indulgence now and then won't hurt at all.

**Odette:** I don't deserve such praise from one so sternly disciplined as you.

**Vodyanitsa:** Oh, you think I don't enough either, do you? Alright then, here, let's get some more food... This is for you, and this is for me...

**Odette:** Stop, stop! That's enough...

#### Wait for a while...

The hour passes fairly quickly, and the group gathers back at the entrance.

**Mitya:** How did it go? I managed to gather a bit of info on my end.

**Valeriy:** Same here.

- **Traveler:** Rather than intel, it's more like we garnered... sponsorship?

You quickly exchange information...

**Mitya:** Allow me to summarize. First, from Valeriy's end: Port Belovodye has seen some recent unrest.

**Mitya:** Port Belovodye isn't exactly a hotbed of unusual incidents, and there are always plenty of explanations for things that deviate only slightly from the norm, so it's never come under scrutiny from up top.

**Valeriy:** Minor incidences sometimes make the best jokes over drinks. So our officers will share them with their colleagues at the right moment, like just now.

**Mitya:** Hmm. On my end, I found that most of the wealthy merchants here didn't react much when I mentioned Snowy Nocturne.

**Mitya:** But when I mentioned that this wine sometimes tastes a bit off, one of them suddenly said he might have tried it as well... Let's just say it left a poor impression.

**Valeriy:** Looks like the bootleg wine has enjoyed quite a wide reach.

**Mitya:** Agreed. Most of those I talked to usually buy their drinks through taverns. But the gentleman who noticed something wrong with the wine had obtained his bottle from a distributor instead.

**Mitya:** Since Mr. Urkin's winery also supplies taverns in Novokitezhgrad, this suggests the real problem may lie with the distributors rather than the taverns.

**Valeriy:** Choosing not to infiltrate taverns, but to enter the market through distributor networks... Quite the cautious approach.

**Mitya:** We suspected they had informants in the taverns earlier. But based on this, the taverns may not be that big a problem, though we can't rule out the possibility completely.

**Valeriy:** Also, the Lord Rooster mentioned to you that I might know where Urkin's reports had gotten blocked?

**Paimon:** Yep, that's what he said.

**Mitya:** He probably didn't want to say anything too blatant at the party. He is the mayor, after all.

**Valeriy:** ...I do have my suspicions.

**Valeriy:** Remember what happened when we first arrived? We encountered that old gentleman, being blocked by two people in uniform who wouldn't let him pass.

**Valeriy:** Those two were from the Royal Railway Transport Bureau. If Urkin encountered any problems, it stands to reason he could have reported them to the Transport Bureau as well.

**Paimon:** So you're saying... You suspect...

**Valeriy:** Wait.

**???:** Oh, no!

**Mitya:** Who's there?

**Valeriy:** Stop him!

The eavesdropper barely manages to run a few steps before you catch up to him. It seems escaping from the likes of you is simply too difficult for someone his age.

**Staranov:** Wait! Wait a minute!

**Mitya:** Well, Mr. Staranov, we meet again! Should we call this an wild coincidence, or is it by design?

**Staranov:** ...Sorry. I was eavesdropping... but I have my reasons.

**Valeriy:** You're related to the Transport Bureau in some way.

**Staranov:** ...Already figured it out, huh? *sigh* No surprise there. I suppose I made it too obvious... I've never been very good at hiding things.

**Valeriy:** And what's your history with the Bureau? Do you have some grudge against them?

**Staranov:** A grudge? Haha... A long time ago, you could say there was no such thing. But somewhere along the way, that was all that remained.

**Staranov:** I used to be a Bureau member. I counted those men amongst my colleagues, once. After I stepped down... they started making things difficult for me.

**Mitya:** That wouldn't have anything to do with your daughter, would it?

**Staranov:** Oh, no, nothing like that. The story about my daughter... I made it up. I'm sorry. I didn't know who you were back then.

**Paimon:** Can't exactly blame you for doing that, though...

**Staranov:** You've been looking for leads, haven't you? Well... I think I can finally share this one with you.

**Staranov:** There's this place just outside Novokitezhgrad that's been bugging me. If you have the time, you can come with me to take a look.

**Mitya:** Do you even have to ask? Let's go.

**Paimon:** Let's move, then!

#### Investigate the suspicious area

**Paimon:** Is this the place? It says "Danger: Energy Leak" here...

**Staranov:** As far as I know, the sign has been here for a long time, and residents rarely get close.

**Mitya:** This is... honestly, a little ridiculous.

**Mitya:** I've seen Novokitezhgrad's energy pipeline map. None of the main lines run through here. And...

**Mitya:** Yeah, just as I thought. There's no sign of an energy leak.

**Paimon:** Good thing we brought an expert.

**Staranov:** Huh? R–Really? This young man's a professional?

**Valeriy:** Mr. Mitya is a researcher with the Energy Commission, providing technical support and consultation for major projects.

**Staranov:** Oh my... I'm so sorry, I should have come clean from the start, then.

**Mitya:** And further confirm that you can't keep secrets? Don't be too hard on yourself, Mr. Staranov. We know you were in a tough spot.

**Staranov:** The reason I left in such a hurry earlier was because I didn't want those men linking you to me. Otherwise, they'd have come after you too.

**Staranov:** I wasn't sure what you were after back then... But... Call me naive, but I kept thinking... what if you were pursuing some hidden truth, just like I was?

**Valeriy:** Do you have anything else you can share with us?

**Staranov:** I... used to be the Transport Bureau Director.

**Mitya:** Oh, dear me. Why didn't you tell us that sooner? That would've saved you a lot of time winning our trust...

**Staranov:** Ah! I've been retired for so long, lad. What's the point of bringing that title up? Besides...

**Staranov:** Above all else, I can't accept what the Bureau has become. Drogin... I've been looking for evidence to bring that bastard down.

**Valeriy:** You mean the current Director? What do you suspect him of?

**Staranov:** Back when I was in charge, Novokitezhgrad's problems were manageable. But ever since he took over... little things have been piling up.

**Staranov:** One of the officers I trained was a young man named Sukhanov. He once told me he suspected Drogin had gangland ties.

**Staranov:** At first, no one believed him. No one dared or wanted to. But Sukhanov was never the type to make baseless accusations, and I wanted to trust him.

**Staranov:** I told him not to draw attention to himself, and to get close to Drogin quietly... to gather evidence first.

**Staranov:** Less than a year later, Sukhanov was killed in the line of duty during an official operation.

**Paimon:** Huh!? Was he silenced, then?

**Staranov:** Maybe. Or maybe Drogin had realized Sukhanov was investigating him, and took the opportunity to nip that thread in the bud.

**Staranov:** I failed Sukhanov. If I hadn't retired, investigating that should've been my job, not his. I...

**Mitya:** No, no, don't say that. Besides, you'd already retired. None of this is on you.

**Valeriy:** I understand how you feel, but please don't blame yourself too much.
